name: Critical material supply risk exposure
description: Supply risk of the raw materials a company's industry runs on - higher means it depends more on materials mined in few, badly governed countries
source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 + World Bank WGI

name: Critical material dependence stated in the 10-K
description: Combined supply risk of the critical materials a company names in its own annual report - higher means it discloses dependence on more, riskier minerals

name: Direct US greenhouse gas emissions per $M revenue
description: Scope 1 CO2e from the company's US facilities above EPA's 25,000 t reporting threshold (GHGRP), ownership-weighted, per $M revenue - how much climate damage the company causes directly for every dollar it earns, so lower is better. 0 = no facility above the threshold (direct US emissions below it), compare within a sector.
source: EPA GHGRP Envirofacts (RLPS_GHG_EMITTER_GAS + PUB_DIM_FACILITY) + SEC XBRL revenue

name: Science-based climate target (SBTi)
description: How ambitious and independently validated a company's emission-reduction target is on the SBTi Target Dashboard (4 net-zero validated, 3 near-term 1.5C, 2 well-below 2C, 1 committed, 0 none/removed) - higher means a credible commitment to cut emissions in line with climate science; measures targets, not actual emissions
source: SBTi Target Dashboard + OpenFIGI ISIN mapping

name: US environmental penalties per $bn revenue (5 years)
description: Federal and state/local penalties assessed in EPA civil enforcement cases (Clean Air/Water Act, hazardous waste, chemicals ...) against the company or its 10-K subsidiaries, settled in the trailing 5 years, per $bn of mean revenue - an official finding that the company harmed or endangered the environment, so lower is better. 0 = no federal EPA penalty found; US federal cases only.
source: EPA ECHO ICIS-FE&C bulk case download (echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads)
